paragraphs: Friend, here's what this passage teaches me: God's word is where you go when life gets hard, and it doesn't wait for the hard to be over. The psalmist says, "This is my comfort in affliction, that Your promise has given me life." (Psalm 119:50) Mockers, ropes, midnight, and he is still holding on to that promise. Comfort doesn't have to wait for easier days.

Then comes the line that gets me every time. "Before I was afflicted, I went astray; but now I keep Your word." (Psalm 119:67) And later, "It was good for me to be afflicted, that I might learn Your statutes." (Psalm 119:71) He doesn't say the pain was fun. He says the LORD was good in it, and he came out knowing God's word better than before. I had some LOUD opinions about my own rough season, and I'm still learning to see it that way.

So what do you do with that, baker? When your own hard season hits, you can reach for God's word like the psalmist did. He ends by saying, "The law from Your mouth is more precious to me than thousands of pieces of gold and silver." (Psalm 119:72) That kind of treasure can't be taken from you by a mocker or a rough night. This psalm isn't finished yet, and I think there's more good stuff coming.
